$comment: Reviewer pool for /adversarial-review (HARNESS-071, #955).
Ordered allow-list of models permitted to SIGN a review.md. The first entry
is the launcher's primary; the whole array is the gate's allow-list, which
dotf spec archive enforces via checkReviewGate.
Standing rule: an adversarial review never runs on an Anthropic model. The
reviewer must not be the implementer, and Claude implements nearly every
change in this repo — BUG-074 was reviewed twice by claude-opus-5 before
anyone noticed, which is the incident this file exists to prevent.
Entries are model IDS, not tool names, and that distinction is load-bearing:
`agy` also serves claude-opus-4-6-thinking and claude-sonnet-4-6, so pinning
the tool would guarantee nothing. Pinning the id does.
`id` is the canonical string a reviewer records in review.md and the gate
matches on. `provider`/`model` are the launcher's flags, kept explicit rather
than parsed out of `id`: BUG-074 round 3 ran on the right model only because
~/.pi/agent/settings.json on one machine happened to default to it — pi's own
default provider is google, and that file is unversioned per-machine state.
A pin that depends on a default is not a pin.
Reasoning-class only. The latency-optimised daily models (nan/qwen3.6,
nan/gemma4, the gemini flash tier) are deliberately absent: a reviewer that
PASSes cheaply is worse than no gate, because it converts the gate into a
green checkmark. This file is read once per spec, so slow is fine.
This is the load-bearing slice of H-044, not a replacement for it. H-044's
model-map.json maps a neutral tier (top|mid|low) to a provider per agent — a
different shape. Kept in a separate file so H-044 need not migrate this one.

pool.why: 1M context and a mandatory reasoning chain — roughly 4x slower than qwen3.6 on trivial prompts, which is the correct trade for a gate that runs once per spec. Exercised: BUG-074 round 3 re-ran the mutation battery itself rather than trusting the spec's table. FLAGGED 2026-08-21 (#1205), not changed: this same model returns a 200 with an EMPTY body under PR-Agent — it spends its OUTPUT budget on the reasoning chain and never writes the answer, measured at 4m15s of silence on kubelab#1202 run 32440498259. That is the behaviour already described in the mimo entry below, from this pool's own harness. PR-Agent's chain was inverted to lead with mimo; this pool's ordering was NOT, because its runner and prompt differ and no measurement of THIS harness exists yet. Read that as an open question about the primary, not as an endorsement of it.

A second provider family, independent of both NaN and Anthropic — provider diversity rather than merely a different model. Pro tier at high effort; the flash tiers are excluded for the same reason qwen3.6 is. agy has no --provider flag; the model id selects the family.

Replaced nan/mimo-v2.5 on 2026-10-01, re-admitted on this file's bar rather than renamed in. NaN retired mimo-v2.5: it answers 401 'This API key does not have access to the requested model' (CI run 36800846902, and a direct call from this repo's key, 2026-10-01), so PR-Agent's primary was dead (#1909). The admission evidence is carried from mlorentedev/dotfiles#1856, not re-derived: given the planted-defect test its predecessor passed (`((count++))` under `set -e`), mimo-v2.6-flash found it, named the failing input (count=0) and gave the fix. That is agreement on one planted defect, not a quality ranking against deepseek. Profile: 1,048,576 context and a reasoning chain (pi's model record; a minimal call here returned reasoning_tokens alongside the answer), which is this pool's line against qwen3.6 and gemma4 at 262K. 'flash' in the name is NaN's naming, not the gemini flash tier this pool excludes; deepseek-v4-flash is admitted on the same profile. Ordering unchanged: a SECOND fallback, after the provider-diverse one, because gemini answers a NaN outage and mimo only answers NaN saturation. In .pr_agent.toml it is the PRIMARY, for the reason in the previous entry's history: its failure mode raises, deepseek's empty 200 does not.
